newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Aeroflot boss says Turin crash still a mystery.
newsitem.headline: Aeroflot boss says Turin crash still a mystery.

text.p: The crash of a giant Antonov-124 freighter in Italy was the result of an "inexplicable situation," a chief executive of Aeroflot-Russian International Airlines said on Wednesday.
Marshal Evgeny Shaposhnikov told reporters that it was still not clear why the crew could not land at Turin airport on Tuesday after their first failed attempt.

"I hope that during next week we will get full information about the reasons for the crash," he said, adding that Russian officials and experts of state aviation organisations were still at the scene.
"The crew (of the plane) met an inexplicable situation and it is not known why they could not get out of it. All the pilots were very experienced," Shaposhnikov said.

The plane's Russian pilot and co-pilot were killed and two villagers died when they were buried in rubble after it sliced into the village of San Francesco al Campo near Turin airport on a flight from Moscow.

Turin prosecutor Bruno Tinti, who is involved in efforts to identify the cause of the crash, told reporters told reporters in Italy earlier that human error may have played a part. "There is certainly a human element," he said.
Shaposhnikov said the plane had two crews of six pilots each on board and a further 11 officials from Ayaks cargo company which owned the plane. All were Russians.
Aeroflot provided its crews to Ayaks, which owns an additional Antonov-124 freighter but does not have the right to operate it.
